one_line_contribution: It makes the retrieved memory item the unit of failure attribution in a multi-step agent, defines item responsibility operationally by seed-replicated removal re-runs (12 seeds, Newcombe interval, plus an emptied-set arm that asks whether memory caused the failure at all), and then uses those labels to measure how often the cheap attributions deployed memory systems actually rely on (self-report, teacher-forced confidence gain, position prior, single-seed LOO) name the same item as a fresh intervention replicate does, at a stated re-run cost.
closest_prior_work: AgenticRAG-FP, 'When Failures Propagate: Causal Failure Attribution in Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation' (arXiv:2608.20627, 2026-08-20; verified with s2cli paper and returned by my query 2 on both HF and S2). It is already an interventional benchmark for failure attribution built exactly the way this proposal builds its E2 arm: inject a certified retrieval fault at a chosen hop, re-execute the downstream trajectory, and score post-hoc diagnosers against the known injected cause, with propagation depth as an evaluation axis. It does not fully collide: its unit is a hop-level retrieval fault in single-episode agentic RAG, not a persistent retrieved experience item; it has no seed replication, no natural-failure labelling (its ground truth is planted, i.e. only the analogue of E2), no non-attributability estimand, and no accuracy-versus-cost frontier. But it removes most of the conceptual novelty of 'intervention as ground truth for attributing an agent failure to a piece of retrieved evidence', and it makes the planted-culprit half of this proposal a re-run of an existing benchmark in a new environment. Second closest: CUE-R (arXiv:2604.05467, verified) already does per-evidence-item REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE with an evidence-role taxonomy, so the intervention primitives and even the duplication manipulation behind P5a are prior art in single-shot RAG; and CausalFlow (arXiv:2605.25338, verified, 8 citations) already does counterfactual causal responsibility scoring for LLM agent failures at step level. What genuinely remains unclaimed after these three is narrow: seed-replicated labels for a stochastic multi-step agent, the fraction of memory-caused failures attributable to no single item, and the measured gap between cheap attributors and an intervention replicate.
strongest_objection: The headline result is close to being manufactured by the selection rule. Episodes enter the scoring pool only if the 12-seed leave-one-out procedure found an item whose removal effect clears r_i ~ 0.33; the ceiling C is a fresh 6-seed run of that same estimator, i.e. the same estimand computed by the same functional form as the label. Pairing and fresh seeds control label noise, which is what the Measurement section argues, but they do not control selection on the estimator: block C is guaranteed to see a large signal on exactly these episodes because that is why they were selected, while self-report, confidence gain, semantic overlap and the position prior are selected on nothing. So P1 (self-report >= 25 points below C) and P2 (confidence gain >= 20 below C) are largely a statement that a re-run of the labelling procedure reproduces its own label better than a different measurement does, on a set defined by that procedure. The reviewer will also note that the method set is a straw man: the actual state of the art in agent failure attribution is an LLM diagnoser over the trajectory (A2P arXiv:2509.10401, ErrorProbe arXiv:2604.17658, CausalFlow arXiv:2605.25338), and the actual attributions deployed memory systems use are learned item scores (MemQ Q-values, usage/survival scores, retrieval similarity) - none of which is scored here. Beating a position prior, a semantic-overlap heuristic and a forced-choice self-report does not establish that 'the cheap attributions current systems rely on' fail. Secondary but concrete: two of the seven predictions cannot be decided by the design as written (the proposal concedes P3b is low-power at +/-11.5 against a 10-point margin; P5b's falsifier sits 2 points above the nominal 10% false-positive rate, far inside the cluster-bootstrap CI, so it measures per-cell power at SE ~0.35, not additivity); P6 is confounded by backbone base rates, since scoring 'reader 2 succeeds at base' as disagreement on episodes selected because reader 1 failed produces the predicted 20-point gap from a base-rate difference alone; and P7's claim that 'regression to the mean is identical in both arms, so only the sentence can produce the gap' is wrong - a procedure sentence that raises p(S) mechanically compresses every r_i by ceiling, which is a second channel to the predicted drop in remain-attributable fraction and is not separated from substitution.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Break the circularity: define the primary scoring set by something other than the label estimator - score all attribution methods on the E2 planted/two-culprit set against the injected oracle as the confirmatory comparison (where the pool is defined by the plant, not by LOO), and demote the natural-episode gaps to a secondary, explicitly selection-caveated analysis; or select the natural pool by the emptied-set criterion (memory-caused) rather than by max_i r_i, and report method accuracy on all memory-caused failures with abstention scored, so a method is not required to reproduce an argmax that only the ceiling's own procedure can produce. (2) Add the two attributors that matter: an LLM post-hoc diagnoser reading the failed trajectory plus the k items (A2P/CausalFlow-style, with an abstain option) and at least one deployed learned item score (retrieval similarity, usage/recency-decay, MemQ-style Q-value) - these are the 'attributions current systems rely on' the abstract names. (3) Fix P6's estimand to label transfer on the subset where reader 2 also fails at base, reporting base-rate mismatch separately. (4) Fix P7 by matching on base success (or reporting r_i normalised by headroom 1 - p(S)) so substitution is separable from ceiling compression. (5) Replace P5b's significance count with a pooled interaction magnitude and CI, and either drop P3b or extend block C to 12 seeds. (6) Cite and position against arXiv:2608.20627 explicitly, and state what the seed-replicated natural-failure labels buy over its injected-fault protocol. (7) Show the labels are worth 54 re-runs each by adding one downstream cell: demote/keep items under each attributor and measure the effect on subsequent success - otherwise this is a diagnostic with no demonstrated consumer.
missing_baseline: Two. First, an LLM failure-diagnoser baseline: give a model the failed trajectory and the k retrieved items and ask it to name the responsible item (with 'none'), in the A2P / ErrorProbe / CausalFlow style - this is the method a reviewer will consider the real competitor to intervention, and the plan's 'self-report' (the actor's own post-episode account) is a much weaker proxy for it. Second, the memory system's own utility scores as attributors: retrieval similarity rank (beyond raw position), usage/recency decay, and one learned per-item score (MemQ-style Q-value or a DIG-style confidence-gain scorer trained on the stream) - the brief's Q1 asks for exactly one scorer per family, and their absence means the paper cannot support its own claim that deployed reinforcement/demotion scores are inaccurate. A cheaper third omission: a random-among-retrieved floor with abstention calibrated to the observed non-attributable rate, so the 'none' option is scored against a matched abstainer rather than against pure random choice.
preprint_collision: No verified collision on the central claim, but the proposal's own check is materially incomplete, and that counts against it. All six of my queries were answered by the literature command (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, both channels ok); WebSearch was unavailable and WebFetch is blocked, so no query used channel (b). Q1 (mechanism, --recent) 'attribute agent failure to responsible retrieved memory item counterfactual removal ground truth benchmark' returned 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap, trajectory-level), 2606.25449, 2509.23735, 2509.10401, 2507.05257, 2606.15903 - none item-level. Q2 (mechanism, --recent) 'interventional benchmark injected fault re-execution ground truth evaluate failure diagnosers retrieval agent' returned arXiv:2608.20627 (AgenticRAG-FP) on both HF and S2, plus AgentDebugX 2607.18754, AgentCheck 2607.11098 (replay with injected faults), 2607.28802, 2601.06112, 2605.25338. Q3 (closest named method) 'leave-one-out intervention per-item utility of retrieved memory items agent episodes seed variance number of re-runs' returned CUE-R 2604.05467 and, notably, 'On Randomness in Agentic Evals' arXiv:2602.07150, which already establishes that single-run agentic estimates are variance-dominated and multiple runs are required - so the seed-replication premise is prior art, not a finding. Q4 (home literature, no agent/memory words) 'data valuation stochastic utility noisy leave-one-out Shapley Monte Carlo retraining variance rank stability' returned Data Shapley 1904.02868, shapiq 2410.01649 and nothing agentic - the seeds-to-label curve is a re-derivation of a known data-valuation phenomenon in a new setting. Q5 (--recent, self-explanation faithfulness) returned 2602.02639, 2502.18156 and 'Thought Branches' 2510.27484 (resampling-based causal analysis of reasoning), confirming the proposal's claim that self-report faithfulness has not been tested against counterfactual re-runs for retrieved items. Q6 (ALFWorld per-item memory ablation) returned VICT 2608.28128, MemHarness 2607.28272, MemQ 2605.08374 - credit at the action or set level, never the item. IDs I verified with s2cli paper or by direct return: 2608.20627, 2605.25338 (8 cit), 2604.05467, 2507.04480 (PKDD/ECML workshops, 7 cit), 2604.17658 (ACL; S2 title 'Towards Self-Improving Error Diagnosis in Multi-Agent Systems', consistent with ErrorProbe), 2509.10401, 2509.23735, 2507.05257, 2607.10608, 2602.02639, 2502.18156. IDs the proposal leans on that I did not verify individually: 2511.20857, 2602.16313, 2605.18565, 2604.20006, 2607.13083, 2401.07927, 2307.08678, 2311.07466. The substantive failure of the proposal's check is that it ran a --recent mechanism query and still missed arXiv:2608.20627, an interventional failure-attribution benchmark with certified injected faults and re-execution that has been on HF since 2026-08-20, three weeks before this brief - it is the nearest neighbour of the E2 arm and it is absent from both the Related Work and the Collision Check, while the check concludes 'no preprint provides item-level responsibility labels with seed replication'. That conclusion survives 2608.20627 on the natural-failure and seed-replication axes, so I do not call this a verified collision, but a novelty claim that missed the closest interventional attribution benchmark in the field has not been established by the proposal's own search - I established what remains of it, and it is narrower than claimed.
